newsitem.title: UK: Sexual radio ad wins UK award for Club 18-30.
newsitem.headline: Sexual radio ad wins UK award for Club 18-30.

text.p: A British package holiday company, Club 18-30, which has been censored for its risqu poster advertising campaigns, received an award on Thursday for its first ever radio ad.
Aerial Awards, which promotes "excellence in radio advertising", said in a statement it gave its monthly award in January to the Club 18-30 ad created by Saatchi & Saatchi.
The ad is about a boy named Colin who "has been a naughty boy and a magazine has been found under his bed". The magazine turns out to be a brochure for Club 18-30.
Andy McGuinness, one of the judges of the competition, said the ad had "a very funny script".
"We liked it because it was a truism of teenage life," he said.
Club 18-30's advertising has attracted a number of complaints from the public about their sexual tone.
Billboard posters last year featured lines such as "Beaver Espana", "The summer of 69" and -- over a picture of a man's torso and bulging boxer shorts -- "packaged holiday".
Britain's Advertising Standards Authority, after receiving complaints about the ads, banned them.
Saatchi & Saatchi changed the ads -- in some cases making them even more overtly sexual -- but dropped the poster campaign and switched the ads to young adult magazines.
